questions: Should the function handle features that are not present in the DataFrame (e.g., raise an error, ignore them, or add them as NaN)?
If a feature column contains NaN values, should the scaler be fitted ignoring NaNs, propagate NaNs, or raise an error?
Should the scaling be applied in-place (modifying the original DataFrame) or return a new DataFrame, and does the function need to avoid side effects on the input?
Is the order of rows in the output required to match the input exactly, or can it be permuted due to scaler operations?
Should the function preserve the original data types of the scaled columns (e.g., convert to float), or is any numeric type acceptable?
If the DataFrame has a custom index (non-integer), must the index be preserved exactly in the output?
Should the function handle duplicate column names in features or the DataFrame?
Is it acceptable to use additional libraries beyond pandas, numpy, and sklearn, or must the implementation be strictly limited to those?
